doc_title: Aflibercept Intravitreal Injection - Medical Necessity
text: Aflibercept is an anti-VEGF agent for specific retinal conditions with confirmed active disease on imaging. Coverage tracks the diagnosis and the imaging evidence, not the drug alone. The patient must have failed or be ineligible for first-line anti-VEGF therapy in many plans; documentation of prior treatments strengthens medical necessity.

doc_title: Aflibercept Intravitreal Injection - Medical Necessity
text: Neovascular age-related macular degeneration with subfoveal or juxtafoveal involvement.

doc_title: Aflibercept Intravitreal Injection - Medical Necessity
text: Diabetic macular edema with central retinal thickness >300 micrometers on OCT.

doc_title: Aflibercept Intravitreal Injection - Medical Necessity
text: Macular edema following a branch or central retinal vein occlusion.

doc_title: Aflibercept Intravitreal Injection - Medical Necessity
text: OCT or fluorescein angiography showing active exudation or fluid in the macular region.

doc_title: Aflibercept Intravitreal Injection - Medical Necessity
text: Document prior anti-VEGF agents (bevacizumab, ranibizumab, brolucizumab) attempted in the same eye, the dates and duration of therapy, the response (improvement, stability, progression), and the reason for switching if applicable. A step-through to aflibercept is not universally required but captured history allows the reviewer to assess medical necessity correctly.

doc_title: Aflibercept Intravitreal Injection - Medical Necessity
text: Active ocular or periocular infection.

doc_title: Aflibercept Intravitreal Injection - Medical Necessity
text: Any indication outside the approved retinal conditions.

doc_title: Upper GI Endoscopy with Biopsy - Medical Necessity
text: Diagnostic upper endoscopy is driven by alarm features or by dyspepsia that has not responded to acid suppression. Age and risk profile matter significantly. For younger patients with uncomplicated dyspepsia, medical management is preferred before invasive evaluation. In older patients or those with red-flag symptoms, endoscopy may be indicated earlier.

doc_title: Upper GI Endoscopy with Biopsy - Medical Necessity
text: Dysphagia (difficulty swallowing) or odynophagia (painful swallowing).

doc_title: Upper GI Endoscopy with Biopsy - Medical Necessity
text: Gastrointestinal bleeding, including melena, hematemesis, or heme-positive stool.

doc_title: Upper GI Endoscopy with Biopsy - Medical Necessity
text: Unintentional weight loss greater than 5% in a short timeframe.

doc_title: Upper GI Endoscopy with Biopsy - Medical Necessity
text: Iron-deficiency anemia with microcytic indices and a positive fecal occult blood.

doc_title: Upper GI Endoscopy with Biopsy - Medical Necessity
text: Dyspepsia that persists after 4-8 weeks of adequate proton pump inhibitor therapy at a standard dose.

doc_title: Upper GI Endoscopy with Biopsy - Medical Necessity
text: For uninvestigated dyspepsia without alarm features, a PPI trial (and H. pylori test-and-treat where relevant) is required first, particularly in patients under age 60. Document the PPI name, dose, start date, end date, and the patient's response or lack thereof. For patients with alarm features, endoscopy may be indicated without a prior PPI trial.

doc_title: Upper GI Endoscopy with Biopsy - Medical Necessity
text: Uninvestigated dyspepsia under age 60 without alarm features and without a PPI trial.

doc_title: Upper GI Endoscopy with Biopsy - Medical Necessity
text: Surveillance endoscopy at an interval shorter than guidelines recommend (usually 3-5 years for uncomplicated findings).

doc_title: Knee Arthroscopy with Meniscectomy - Medical Necessity
text: Arthroscopic partial meniscectomy helps patients whose knee mechanically locks, catches, or gives way because of a symptomatic meniscal tear. Multiple randomized trials show it does not reliably outperform structured physical therapy for degenerative meniscal change or osteoarthritis without true mechanical symptoms, so separating a mechanically unstable knee from painful arthritis is the decision that matters and the note should make that distinction explicit.

doc_title: Knee Arthroscopy with Meniscectomy - Medical Necessity
text: Mechanical symptoms (locking, catching, true giving way, or an inability to fully extend the knee) that persist despite conservative treatment.

doc_title: Knee Arthroscopy with Meniscectomy - Medical Necessity
text: MRI or a positive provocative exam (for example a positive McMurray) consistent with a meniscal tear that correlates with the patient's symptoms.

doc_title: Knee Arthroscopy with Meniscectomy - Medical Necessity
text: Effusion or joint-line tenderness localizing to the involved compartment.

doc_title: Knee Arthroscopy with Meniscectomy - Medical Necessity
text: Expect a documented trial of physical therapy, activity modification, and analgesics or anti-inflammatories over roughly three months before surgery, with dates and the response recorded. A locked knee that cannot be straightened is the exception and may proceed without the full conservative course. Vague statements such as "failed conservative care" without dates route to the reviewer.

doc_title: Knee Arthroscopy with Meniscectomy - Medical Necessity
text: Isolated degenerative osteoarthritis or a degenerative tear without mechanical symptoms.

doc_title: Knee Arthroscopy with Meniscectomy - Medical Necessity
text: No trial of conservative care in the prior three months and no locked knee.

doc_title: Knee Arthroscopy with Meniscectomy - Medical Necessity
text: Advanced tricompartmental arthritis where arthroplasty is the appropriate step.

doc_title: MRI Lumbar Spine - Medical Necessity
text: Lumbar MRI is a diagnostic step, not a screening test. It is indicated when a patient has completed a meaningful trial of conservative care and still has symptoms that would change management if a structural cause were found.

doc_title: MRI Lumbar Spine - Medical Necessity
text: Radicular pain or neurologic deficit persisting or worsening after >= 6 weeks of physical therapy, NSAIDs, or activity modification.

doc_title: MRI Lumbar Spine - Medical Necessity
text: Red-flag features (suspected malignancy, infection, cauda equina, or trauma) at any time, which override the waiting period.

doc_title: MRI Lumbar Spine - Medical Necessity
text: Document the type of conservative care, the start and end dates, and the response. A vague statement such as "tried PT" without dates is treated as incomplete evidence and should route to the reviewer rather than an automated approval.

doc_title: MRI Lumbar Spine - Medical Necessity
text: Acute uncomplicated low back pain of less than 6 weeks with no red flags.

doc_title: MRI Lumbar Spine - Medical Necessity
text: A repeat study within 12 months when nothing clinically has changed.

doc_title: Attended Polysomnography - Medical Necessity
text: Attended in-lab polysomnography is reserved for patients who cannot be evaluated reliably with a home sleep apnea test, or whose home test was technically inadequate or negative despite a strong clinical picture. Home testing is the default first study for uncomplicated suspected obstructive sleep apnea because it is cheaper and more accessible. Much of this policy turns on clinical judgment about pretest probability and comorbidity, so borderline cases with thin documentation belong with a human reviewer rather than an automated decision.

doc_title: Attended Polysomnography - Medical Necessity
text: Symptoms of obstructive sleep apnea (habitual snoring, witnessed apneas, gasping arousals, excessive daytime sleepiness) with at least moderate pretest probability, ideally supported by a validated screening tool such as STOP-BANG or the Epworth Sleepiness Scale.

doc_title: Attended Polysomnography - Medical Necessity
text: A comorbidity (moderate-to-severe heart failure, significant chronic lung disease, prior stroke, or neuromuscular disease) that makes home testing unreliable.

doc_title: Attended Polysomnography - Medical Necessity
text: A prior negative or technically failed home sleep study with persistent symptoms.

doc_title: Attended Polysomnography - Medical Necessity
text: There is no medication step. The gate is whether a home study is a reasonable first test. If the note does not address that question, or does not record a screening score or a qualifying comorbidity, the criteria are indeterminate and the request should be interpreted against this guidance rather than auto-decided.

doc_title: Attended Polysomnography - Medical Necessity
text: Home sleep apnea testing is appropriate and no disqualifying comorbidity exists.

doc_title: Attended Polysomnography - Medical Necessity
text: Repeat study within 12 months without a change in weight, symptoms, or therapy.

doc_title: Lumbar Transforaminal Epidural Steroid Injection - Medical Necessity
text: A lumbar transforaminal epidural steroid injection targets an inflamed nerve root that imaging confirms is compressed and that explains the patient's leg pain. The procedure delivers medication directly to the site of nerve compression, providing local anti-inflammatory effect. It is a bridge therapy, not a long-term solution; cumulative injections and patient age must be considered.

doc_title: Lumbar Transforaminal Epidural Steroid Injection - Medical Necessity
text: Dermatomal radicular pain (sharp, shooting, burning leg pain in a single nerve distribution) matching an imaging-confirmed level of nerve root compression.

doc_title: Lumbar Transforaminal Epidural Steroid Injection - Medical Necessity
text: At least four weeks of conservative therapy (physical therapy, NSAIDs, muscle relaxants, activity modification) without adequate relief.

doc_title: Lumbar Transforaminal Epidural Steroid Injection - Medical Necessity
text: MRI, CT, or other structural imaging confirming disk herniation, stenosis, or foraminal narrowing at the symptomatic level.

doc_title: Lumbar Transforaminal Epidural Steroid Injection - Medical Necessity
text: Document the dates and types of conservative measures, pain scores before and after conservative care, any improvement or plateau, and the specific imaging findings. Track all prior injections at the same level and the dates; more than three in a rolling twelve months falls outside policy and should be flagged. A gap of at least 12 weeks between injections at the same level is typical.

doc_title: Lumbar Transforaminal Epidural Steroid Injection - Medical Necessity
text: Systemic infection (bacteremia, sepsis) or active bleeding diathesis.

doc_title: Lumbar Transforaminal Epidural Steroid Injection - Medical Necessity
text: A fourth or subsequent same-level injection within a rolling twelve-month period.

doc_title: Lumbar Transforaminal Epidural Steroid Injection - Medical Necessity
text: Anticoagulation that cannot be safely interrupted or bridged.
